bull_case: Meta's user graph, creator inventory, advertiser demand, conversion data and AI ranking reinforce each other across billions of daily users. Rising ad price and impressions suggest the moat is currently strengthening.
bear_case: Users and advertisers can multi-home, frontier models may commoditize, and regulation can restrict data advantages. TikTok, Google and new AI-native interfaces can intercept discovery and advertiser intent.
thesis: The moat is strengthening on observable monetization and ecosystem metrics, not merely narrative. Meta has scale, growth and multiple feedback loops between users, creators, advertisers and ranking data. The network/data criterion reaches 85 because several primary metrics show scale and trend, but there is no hard switching-cost lock. Commoditization risk is moderated by distribution and proprietary interaction data rather than eliminated.

evidence.claim: Family DAP averaged 3.60B in June 2026, up 3% YoY, providing massive user and content-network scale.
Ad impressions rose 12% and average price per ad 9% in FY2025; Q2 2026 showed 14% impressions and 12% price growth, indicating simultaneous inventory and monetization expansion.
Meta reported AI ranking changes that increased Facebook ad clicks 8.3% and conversions 15.7%, demonstrating that interaction and ad data can be converted into measurable performance improvements.

Meta's 10-Q states that competing products have reduced engagement for some users, particularly younger demographics, and that Reels monetizes below Feed/Stories, confirming real substitution pressure.

counterevidence: User and advertiser switching costs are behavioral rather than contractual; both groups can multi-home.
Generative and frontier AI models may become broadly available, reducing differentiation at the model layer.
Privacy and competition regulation can directly weaken targeting and data-combination advantages.
Attention competition remains intense, especially among younger users.
unknowns: No frozen third-party market-share series quantifies Meta's share of global digital advertising through 2026.
The durability of Meta's proprietary-data advantage as synthetic data and general-purpose models improve is not directly measurable.
falsifiers: DAP, impression growth and price per ad all weaken while competitors gain engagement.
Advertiser conversion uplift from proprietary ranking models disappears as industry models commoditize.
A major privacy or platform rule materially reduces targeting performance and persists without recovery.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Current observable moat metrics are not shrinking: DAP, ad impressions, price per ad and reported AI conversion performance are all positive. Future substitution risk is monitored in score/uncertainty rather than treated as present persistent shrinkage.

key_kpis.name: Ad price and conversion uplift
key_kpis.threshold: positive pricing with measurable advertiser ROI

next_checks: Add third-party digital-ad market share to distinguish industry growth from moat-driven share gain.
Track advertiser adoption and performance of Meta's AI stack versus competing ad platforms.
Reassess data/network advantages after material privacy or AI regulation.

subscores.rationale: Pricing and impression growth are both positive, supporting a strengthening monetization position. Low contractual switching costs and intense competition keep the score at the 75 strengthening anchor rather than 90.

Primary metrics provide at least three ecosystem-scale/trend observations: 3.60B DAP, rising impressions and rising ad price, with additional measured AI conversion uplift. The observable row is 85 because scale plus same-definition growth is confirmed, but concrete hard switching costs are not.

Distribution, social graphs, advertiser relationships and proprietary interaction data create multiple defensive layers against model commoditization, matching the 75 anchor; regulation and multi-homing prevent 90.

uncertainties.rationale: Pricing power is observable, but direct advertiser switching-cost data are not disclosed.
Several scale metrics are visible; causal attribution from data scale to future model edge remains imperfect.
Frontier-model commoditization and regulation could shift value away from Meta's model/data layer.
